angle: Instead of jumping to code or multivariate theory, this one performs gradient descent by hand on three points of weight-height data, deriving the loss derivative with the chain rule and walking shrinking steps from an intercept-only warm-up to a two-parameter gradient.
angle_detail: Start with [09:41]–[14:05] for the worked intercept descent with its slope, learning-rate, and stopping rules, then move to [14:49]–[19:14] for partial derivatives and the gradient step. It states least squares and linear regression as prerequisites and is candid that a large learning rate can fail, so note the 0.01 choice there rather than copying the earlier 0.1. Stochastic descent gets only a closing sketch, so bring another source for large-scale practice.
